name: Amendments by the committee responsible – put to the vote collectively
title: REPORT on the proposal for a Council decision amending Decision (EU) 2021/1764 on the Association of the Overseas Countries and Territories with the European Union including relations between the European Union on the one hand, and Greenland and the Kingdom of Denmark on the other

part_text: (10a) As the world's largest island and with a strategic position in the Arctic region, Greenland provides the Union with opportunities to strengthen its political role in the region as it plays a vital role in an area of intensifying geopolitical competition, climate change-driven transformations and emerging shipping routes, evidenced by the growing external pressure and unfounded territorial claims it currently faces. / (10b) In particular, Greenland constitutes one of the extremes of the Greenland-Iceland-United Kingdom (GIUK) gap, a strategic corridor critical for European maritime domain awareness. Control of the North Atlantic sea lanes and the detection and deterrence of hybrid threats is therefore increasingly important, also in light of initiatives such as Polar Connect and Vision 2030, which envisage submarine cable routes linking Greenland and Iceland to continental Europe. Ensuring the security of such undersea infrastructure, including cables and associated digital ecosystems, against sabotage, espionage and physical disruption, requires close and coordinated joint action between the EU, NATO allies and Arctic partners. Moreover, as foreign information manipulation and interference (FIMI) directed at Arctic and North Atlantic communities poses a distinct and growing threat to public resilience, democratic debate and situational awareness in the region, a comprehensive approach to the security of the GIUK corridor must integrate not only maritime surveillance and military deterrence but also the protection of critical infrastructure and the defence of the information environment through shared standards, early-warning mechanisms and coordinated counter-FIMI measures. / (10c) Greenland also has significant unexploited reserves of critical raw materials, including manganese and graphite, and possesses significant potential for renewable and hydroelectric energy. Those reserves, together with those of other OCTs, notably New Caledonia with its significant nickel resources, could enhance the Union’s strategic autonomy and contribute to reducing dependencies on third countries. In addition, Greenland offers unique advantages for the development of the Union's space policy, including space access, ground infrastructure and research capabilities. Its geographic positioning provides strategic opportunities for satellite deployment, tracking and data collection, thereby contributing to the Union's technological sovereignty and autonomy in space. Any excavation of Greenlandic resources needs to be conducted in a sustainable manner and in close cooperation with the Greenlandic people. Greenland is already experiencing the severe impact of climate change, including accelerating ice sheet melt, coastal erosion and changing marine ecosystems. / (10d) Support for EU accession is increasing among Greenlanders and the importance of respecting the sovereignty, territorial integrity and self-determination of Greenland as an autonomous constituent country within the Kingdom of Denmark is paramount, as Greenland’s people firmly reject any external attempts to alter that status without their free will and consent. The Union and its partners should therefore support Denmark and Greenland in safeguarding the region’s stability in the face of external geopolitical pressures, including through enhanced Arctic cooperation. / (10f) Cooperation with Greenland should ensure that the Union remains a strategic, reliable and trusted partner in a context of growing international interest in the region, while the sustainable development of Greenland must fully respect the rights, livelihoods and traditional knowledge of local and indigenous communities, and should ensure their meaningful participation in decisions concerning resource extraction. The Commission and the Member States should also support the development of high-quality higher education institutions and an integrated education-to-employment framework in Greenland. / ‘(b) to support and to cooperate with Greenland in addressing its major challenges such as direct threats to its sovereignty as well as to support Greenlanders by raising education level and economic diversification, and to contribute to the capacity of the administration of Greenland to formulate and implement national policies, including in areas related to economic governance, infrastructure development and strategic resource management, while strengthening resilience, self-sufficiency and safeguarding critical infrastructure.’; / ‘(a) an OCTs-EU forum for dialogue (the ‘OCTs-EU Forum’), which shall meet every year to bring together OCTs’ authorities, representatives of the Member States, the Commission and the European Parliament. Representatives of the EIB and representatives of the outermost regions shall, where appropriate, be associated with the OCTs-EU Forum; / (e) while ensuring the highest standards of environmental protection, biodiversity conservation and ecosystem integrity, particularly in Arctic environments; / (m) the development of regional cooperation in the Arctic, the Caribbean, the Indian Ocean, the Atlantic and the Pacific, including in the areas of secure connectivity, maritime safety and security, emergency preparedness and disaster response, research and innovation, and the protection of critical infrastructure, as well as by strengthening the Union's presence, its capacity for cooperation with third-country partners and the protection of its strategic interests in those spaces; / (iii a) respond to strategic, security or sovereignty needs, in particular to strengthen the Union’s role in sensitive geopolitical areas or those subject to attempts at foreign interference, protect critical infrastructure and support the OCTs’ surveillance and resilience capacities. / 1a.
